title: Jon Rahm’s Ryder Cup future in question with no DP World Tour settlement
content:
Jon Rahm’s availability for the 2027 Ryder Cup is now in serious doubt as the Spaniard continues to resist any financial penalty related to his 2023 departure to LIV Golf.

The DP World Tour announced Saturday that eight golfers have paid all of their fines related to breaking the European-based tour’s regulations (playing on LIV) and are thus free from any further disciplinary action. That list includes Tyrrell Hatton, a member of the European Ryder Cup team last fall that won in New York, as well as future Ryder Cup hopefuls Tom McKibbin, David Puig, Thomas Detry, Laurie Canter, Adrian Meronk and Viktor Perez. Australian Elvis Smylie, one of LIV’s newest adds and winner of its first event this year, was also on the list.

In addition to paying outstanding fines, the group of eight agreed to participate in additional DP World Tour tournaments, “as well as associated media activity and promotion.” They have all dropped their appeals as well.

Notably absent from the list was Rahm, a two-time major winner and one of the best players in the world. He played in all five matches at Bethpage Black, winning three points for the Euros.

LIV Golf initially paid the fines for its players; Rahm has said his total is up to $3 million. But LIV walked back that policy, leaving it to its players to settle the issue with the DP World Tour directly.

Some, including Sergio Garcia, Ian Poulter and Lee Westwood, have given up or resigned their membership to the tour they have been members of since the beginning of their professional careers. Rahm and Hatton filed an appeal to the DP World Tour over the issue in late 2024, which has not been ruled on. That kept them eligible for 2025’s Ryder Cup but if the ruling goes against Rahm, he’s in danger of missing out in 2027 at Adare Manor in Ireland.

“They are not precedent-setting,” the DP World Tour said in a statement of the releases granted to the other. “Requests for releases will continue to be considered on their individual merits in accordance with the Regulations that all members agree to abide by.”

That money could break up the dynamic captain Luke Donald has created with the Europeans did not go unnoticed by another of its stars.

“We went really hard on the Americans about being paid to play the Ryder Cup,” Rory McIlroy said last month. “We also said that we would pay to play in Ryder Cups. There’s two guys that can prove it.”
